title: feat(host): add ace demo with scripted teammates and mocked data
body:
Adds `ace demo`, a self-contained way to show Ace with nothing of yours: a made-up `beats-demo` drum machine project with two seeded channels, `delay-effect` (adding a tempo-synced delay) and `synthwave-theme` (restyling the sequencer), and the teammates idan and davidslater (real GitHub accounts, so their avatars and names load from GitHub), who open channels, type, talk, react and ask the channel agent on a 15-second loop.

- `ace demo [--port 4150]` reruns `ace serve --loopback --demo` as a child process in a temporary home (`ACE_HOME`, `ACE_CONFIG_HOME`, its own keychain service) and removes the home when it stops. Catalog and keys read their home and identity when they load, so it needs its own process.
- Agents use a faux `demo/agent` model (pi-ai `fauxProvider`). Script `ask` steps can carry a `reply` and `thinking`, and anything off-script gets a note that this is a demo. No keys or models are used, and captions and recaps are skipped because no real model is available.
- The demo host has its own tailnet, skips the Tailscale watcher, and refuses to call `gh`. Otherwise the real GitHub account's avatar showed up next to the made-up people.
- `importSeed` takes a seed object and a `shared` option, so the teammates' asks are admitted.
- The viewer is `ghost`, GitHub's deleted-user placeholder, so no real person's avatar appears.
- `docs/demo.md` documents `ace demo` and the `reply`/`thinking` fields.

To try it from a checkout: `bun app build && bun ace demo`, then open the printed sign-in link.

Validation:
- `bun types`: passed
- `bun run ci`: passed (0 errors, the 7 warnings already on main)
- Smoke test of `bun ace demo`:
  - seeding, the script steps (no `demo.step.failed`), the scripted agent reply with thinking, and the off-script reply all checked in the browser;
  - a process-group Ctrl-C exits 0 and removes the temporary home.
- Not tested: the packaged app's `ace demo` (`config.cli = [execPath]` with `argv0`).

### Built in Ace

No. Built in the GitHub Copilot app (Copilot CLI agent) on a Mac, and checked in its browser panel against the demo host. Pushed with `git push` instead of `lane push` because `lane` isn't installed on this machine. The commit has a `Why:` trailer for `lane` to promote later.
